newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong ferry collision injures at least 27.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong ferry collision injures at least 27.

text.p: A high-speed catamaran ferry bound for China collided with a car ferry in Hong Kong waters on Tuesday injuring at least 27 people, government officials said.
Rescue operations were under way and catamaran passengers were being transferred to the car ferry, a government information officer said. Further details were not immediately available.

The catamaran ferry Haiyang, believed to be Chinese-owned, had 129 passengers and crew on board and was sailing to the south China city of Zhuhai, adjacent to Macau on the Pearl River estuary, when it collided with the ferry.
The accident happened near Hong Kong's new airport, currently under construction off the coast of Lantau Island. Police launches and firefighting boats rushed to the spot.
Live television showed the second vessel was a roll-on roll-off car ferry. Its routing at the time of the accident was not immediately available.
It was the second collision in a week involving a Zhuhai-bound high-speed ferry out of Hong Kong.
Last Wednesday a similar vessel, the Hoi Bin, carrying 193 passengers, collided with a small Chinese junk.
Nobody was seriously hurt in that incident.
